title: Bindings, not variables
summary: let creates an immutable binding by default; mut opts into change; shadowing rebinds a name.
lecture: Rust calls them bindings, not variables, because by default they do not vary. `let x = 5;` binds a name to a value, and reassigning it is a compile error. If you want mutation, you say so up front with `let mut`. Reading Rust, `mut` is a signal: this value changes somewhere below.

Shadowing is the second tool: a new `let` with the same name creates a fresh binding, and the old one stops being visible. Unlike mutation, shadowing can change the type - parse a `&str` into an `i32` and keep the same name. It is idiomatic, not a trick.
`const` is for values fixed at compile time. It requires an explicit type, lives happily at the top level, and is named in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE by convention.

example.code:
let spelled = "three";
let spelled = 3;       // shadowing: new binding, new type
example.caption: The second let replaces the first for the rest of the scope.
